title: Klunk paper
description: An exam paper as a selection of bank questions, never as a copy of them. Editing a question in the bank updates every paper that uses it, and the same question can never silently diverge between two papers.

profileId.description: The profile whose rules this paper is checked against. Without it Klunk can still print the paper but cannot tell you the marks are wrong.

school.description: What goes on the cover of this paper in particular. The school's own name and logo live in the folder's school.json; these are the per-paper facts, plus overrides for the two branding fields where one paper genuinely differs.

name.description: Overrides school.json for this paper alone, e.g. a campus that prints its own name.

logoFile.description: Overrides school.json's logo for this paper alone. Path relative to the paper file, not to school.json, because that is where it sits.

status.description: 'used' means it has been sat. Klunk warns before reusing questions from a used paper, which is the mistake that actually happens in a faculty.

profileSectionId.description: Which profile section this fills, so per-section mark and count rules can be checked.

refs.description: Questions in the order they appear on the paper.

oneOf.description: Shorthand: 'bank/design-processes.json#q14', meaning question id q14 in that file, relative to the content folder.

marksOverride.description: Use the question but score it differently here. Recorded on the paper, never written back to the bank.

group.description: A heading printed above this question, and above every one after it until another group is named. The 2025 Visual Arts trial heads the pairs of alternatives in its Section II 'Practice', 'Conceptual Framework' and 'Frames', which is how a student choosing one finds it. Held on the paper rather than on the question, because the same question can be filed under a different heading on another paper.
